questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: As my major is Japan studies, going abroad to Japan is the obvious choice. I specifically wanted to go to improve my spoken abilities, so I wanted to be submerged in the language.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Once I arrived everything was easy to figure out.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got access to the last needed information, but I'm not sure if that counts?

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I was expecting more in-person orientation. I felt a little overlooked, especially before arriving, as the number of short term exchange students seemed pretty low and most international students seemed to last the entire semester. Covid was probably a factor, as it was very hard to get a visa for Japan, so most people didn't expect to be able to go.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I sent my application to the university, that assigned me a partner association, so I sent them an application and they assigned me to a dorm. The partner association was pretty slow with answering at times, but that was my main problem.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Despite living off campus, I lived within walking of the university, so it was very easy.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: If your dorm has sunako beds, seriously consider investing in a mattress.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Oh boy. There were tears. If the university had described some tips and tricks for the system instead of just a how to, it would have been pretty simple and painless, but without that I got really stressed over how unlucky I was.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There are three rounds of registration. In the first two rounds you can apply to classes and drop them, while in the third round you can only drop classes at my department. (I was not aware of the detail about the third round until very late). (For Japanese classes you could thankfully still add in the last round.) If you know how to play the system, you apply to every single interesting class in the first round instead of only taking the required number. This is especially true for Japanese classes that fill up quickly. It very quickly becomes a very stressful gamble if you only try to cover your holes and don't overcommit initially.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was a list of number of spots left (that I only found prior to the third round), but even though I came to them in tears, the administrators were unable or unwilling to promise me a spot (or promise to only give me one spot even if I applied to plenty in the last round). All they did was help me find classes that seemed unlikely to fill up.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Despite all that stress, I'm pretty satisfied with the classes I ended up with. The main problem initially was that three of the four most interesting classes were at the same time, so I had to find some back ups.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Apply to every single interesting class in the first round instead of only taking the required number. Then you can whittle it down in the next two rounds. If you don't get your most desired class in the first round, you can non-stressfully apply again in the second (others may have dropped it), if you know you have enough credits to cover your requirements already.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was pretty good.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was comparable.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was a lot more student led presentations. I really, really enjoyed that we could work on our grades during the semester as it made exam period way less stressful.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Language and Society, Language and Mind, Structure of Language, Discuss Documentary and News Programs in Japanese, Analyzing Japan through Public Advertisement

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: They were all great! You can't transfer the Japanese classes if you're a MA student, though. As the Japanese department isn't at MA level, it doesn't count, even if you take the advanced classes.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had to go to a doctor and that actually costs money there.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I was expecting to find more places with cheap, fun clothing, but all of the cool stuff was really expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Lots of clubs were available! Especially if you speak Japanese.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Absolutely see if you can join a club.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Everywhere

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I had been on exchange in Japan before, so I knew what I was getting into.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Put yourself out there. Clubs are great, because then you can force yourself to go, even if it's hard.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: My main cultural challenge was wondering if I was unknowingly being offensive. I didn't think too much about differences on a cultural level, rather on a personal one.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: There's a lot of order and enough people that things have to be done right. There's also enough people that a lot of weird and amazing types of experiences are financially sound.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Figure out the strategy for applying for classes before you go into it.
2. You can get far with katakana, even if you don't speak any Japanese
3. Enjoy living in Tokyo!!!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I got the official acceptance letter from my department and dorm what felt pretty shortly before I left because of the difference in semester timing.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I have many friendships completely in Japanese now

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Time difference and distance to my friends. It's easy to feel alone when you're on the other side of the world and that's completely okay.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I look forwards to going back

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
